ios.desc:
Due remembers all the things that you need so you don't have to.

It reminds you again and again until you act, so it’s impossible to forget anything.

And it's lightning-fast to set and postpone reminders, all thanks to a clever time picker and natural date parsing.


KEY FEATURES

1. Persistent & Effective
Auto Snooze* keeps nudging you about a missed reminder until you mark it done or reschedule it. Choose between every 1, 5, 10, 15, 30 and 60 minutes.

2. Impossible to Miss
Some reminders can't wait. Use Critical Alerts to get through silent mode and Focus. Or use Prominent Alerts†, which ring like an alarm until you act.

3. Fast to Set, Fast to Postpone
Keep the times you use most a tap away. Twelve Quick Access Times—all fully customizable—make setting or postponing reminders a piece of cake.

4. Just Type or Say It
Type or say “Dentist 3p Thu” or “Meeting in 1h 20m”. Due spots the date, and one tap sets it.

5. Powerful Recurring Reminders
From simple daily reminders to the every-3rd-Wednesday-of-the-month kind, Due keeps up with your routine.

6. Countdown Timers
Not every reminder happens at a time of day. Some happen when the laundry cycle is done. That's what timers are for: precise to the second, with Auto Snooze too. Or just say “Hey Siri, start Laundry timer in Due”.

7. On Your Apple Watch
Wear an Apple Watch? Due comes with you. Mark reminders done, snooze them, add new ones, start and stop timers—all from your wrist. It's a companion to Due on iPhone, so keep your iPhone nearby.

8. Widgets, Control Center & Shortcuts
See what's coming up on your Home Screen and Lock Screen. Start timers and add reminders from Control Center, and automate the rest with Shortcuts.

9. Everywhere You Are
Your reminders and timers on your iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Mac‡, all kept in sync with iCloud or Dropbox.

10. No Account, Completely Private
There's no account to sign up for. We don't store, and we can't access, your reminders and timers. And you don't need internet to receive reminders.

11. Accessible to Everyone
Due follows the text size you set on your device, on every screen, and offers full VoiceOver support. It's also localized in 17 languages.


* By default, auto snooze repeats 5 times, and can be configured to repeat up to 10 times. Due can auto snooze any overdue items indefinitely when you launch Due or act on any of its notifications.
† Prominent Alerts require iOS 26 or later.
‡ Sync on Mac requires Due for Mac (sold separately).


WHAT

If you truly want something naggingly persistent, the Due app [1][2] is very full-featured and has an "auto snooze" feature that allows you to have a reminder send you a push notification e.g., every 10 minutes, indefinitely.

quotes.story_title: Show HN: I built an app to create repeatable checklists to help with ADHD

quotes.text:
I have ADHD and hence am generally quite interested in apps in this space.

Maybe it's just me but I found the app controls to be way too small, too many onboarding walk through steps and way too much information density in the Task screen.

Progress, Highlight, Due Date, different lists - it's a lot.

It seems to me you wanted to pack a punch, but it's so dense and so many steps involved that it falls into the productivity fallacy for me: It's increasing my executive disfunction and makes it harder and cumbersome to add tasks instead of reducing it.

One app that really works for me, does one thing and does it well is for example Due: https://apps.apple.com/de/app/due-erinnerungen-timer/id390017969

Not affiliated in any way with the app or it's creator.

When it comes to apps like these, less is more for me.
quotes.story_title: Show HN: I built a task manager that separates "do" and "due" dates

quotes.text:
For anyone on Android, I never missed any task when I was using COL Reminder [0] which has repeat reminders until you mark something done.

Now I'm using iOS the closest I've found is Due [1] but it's exactly like you said, iPhone notifications are more transient and I have missed stuff.

> The system would be able to nag me more if I do not ack

This is where iOS isn't great, Due seems to get silenced or killed off if it creates too many notifications. So it would be better if there was a nagging service running somewhere else than the phone itself. Maybe an email based nag service would work, something that when a task is due it sends an email every hour until you reply saying "done" or "snooze 1 day" or whatever.

edit: Found an email based nag service - https://www.followupthen.com/how#tasks

[0]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.colapps.reminder&hl=en_US&gl=US

[1]: https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/due-reminders-timers/id390017969
